scope: Main tabular threat families; deliberately not an exhaustive list of all known exploits.

attacks.name: Direct identifiers
attacks.summary: Names and contact details identify people without statistical tricks.
attacks.implemented: Field-name and pattern scans; masks, drops and keyed pseudonyms.
attacks.mitigation: Review all fields; remove unnecessary identifiers. Pseudonyms still permit linkage.
attacks.limitation: Heuristics miss names and unfamiliar formats.

attacks.name: Quasi-identifier uniqueness
attacks.summary: Age, location and body measurements can form a distinctive combination.
attacks.implemented: Exact equality-class sizes on explicitly chosen fields.
attacks.mitigation: Generalize or remove unnecessary identifying precision.
attacks.limitation: Sample uniqueness is not population identification probability.

attacks.name: Record linkage
attacks.summary: Outside knowledge can point to a matching protected record.
attacks.implemented: Verified exact-match replay for internally transformed data with private scoring lineage.
attacks.mitigation: Reduce distinguishing attributes and test stronger attacker knowledge.
attacks.limitation: No external identity database or fuzzy-match calibration is included.

attacks.name: Homogeneity / attribute disclosure
attacks.summary: Everyone in a plausible matching group may share the same sensitive fact.
attacks.implemented: Distinct-l and homogeneous-group diagnostics.
attacks.mitigation: Protect sensitive distributions, not just group sizes.
attacks.limitation: Semantic similarity between different medical labels is not modeled.

attacks.name: Skewness and similarity
attacks.summary: A group can have multiple labels yet overwhelmingly suggest one condition.
attacks.implemented: Categorical total-variation shift from the released-table distribution.
attacks.mitigation: Consider a vetted t-closeness or related model with meaningful category distances.
attacks.limitation: This diagnostic is not general t-closeness enforcement.

attacks.name: Background-knowledge inference
attacks.summary: An attacker may already know more than the fields you selected.
attacks.implemented: Editable known/secret roles and warnings for excluded quasi-identifiers.
attacks.mitigation: Evaluate multiple plausible knowledge profiles.
attacks.limitation: Unknown outside knowledge cannot be exhaustively enumerated.

attacks.name: Missingness fingerprints
attacks.summary: The pattern of blank tests can itself distinguish a patient or imply a diagnosis.
attacks.implemented: Nulls participate in equality classes; missing-rate utility comparisons.
attacks.mitigation: Review missingness as information, not harmless empty space.
attacks.limitation: Clinical meaning of missing tests is not inferred.

attacks.name: Rare subgroup exposure
attacks.summary: Rare combinations can remain identifying after names disappear.
attacks.implemented: Small equality-class diagnostics and suppression.
attacks.mitigation: Review tails and rare cohorts separately; measure suppression bias.
attacks.limitation: No population-frequency model or rare-genome analysis.

attacks.name: Membership inference
attacks.summary: A release may reveal whether a person was in a study.
attacks.implemented: Catalog and adapter boundary only; no built-in calibrated membership attacker.
attacks.mitigation: Use independent member/nonmember evaluation and appropriate formal mechanisms.
attacks.limitation: Not assessed must never appear as a passed test.

attacks.name: Synthetic-data inference
attacks.summary: Fake rows can still reveal facts learned from real participants.
attacks.implemented: Optional Anonymeter inference adapter with independent-control requirements.
attacks.mitigation: Audit generation provenance, controls, attack baselines and uncertainty.
attacks.limitation: Adapter was not installed or runtime-verified in this delivery.

attacks.name: Exact and near-copy memorization
attacks.summary: A synthetic generator may reproduce unusual training examples.
attacks.implemented: A future copy-distance audit is specified.
attacks.mitigation: Test holdout-calibrated attacks, not distance alone.
attacks.limitation: Nearest-neighbor distance is not a privacy guarantee.

attacks.name: Cross-release intersection
attacks.summary: Different coarse releases can become precise when combined.
attacks.implemented: Computed synthetic 3-by-3 composition counterexample.
attacks.mitigation: Review release history and alignment keys together.
attacks.limitation: General multi-release attacker is not implemented.

attacks.name: Aggregate differencing
attacks.summary: Subtract two large, overlapping statistics to expose a small difference.
attacks.implemented: Computed synthetic count/sum counterexample.
attacks.mitigation: Limit release surfaces; prefer a correctly accounted DP query service when suitable.
attacks.limitation: Naive small-cell suppression and pairwise checks do not stop every attack.

attacks.name: Database reconstruction
attacks.summary: Enough statistical constraints can determine hidden individual values.
attacks.implemented: Described threat; no general reconstruction solver shipped.
attacks.mitigation: Restrict exact query workloads or use carefully composed DP.
attacks.limitation: A query-result scanner alone cannot certify safety.

attacks.name: Repeated-query noise averaging
attacks.summary: Repeated noisy answers can be averaged to recover an accurate statistic.
attacks.implemented: Budget design and regression-test requirements documented.
attacks.mitigation: Use one global accountant and a deliberate cache/requery policy.
attacks.limitation: The optional in-memory DP demonstration is not a persistent service.

attacks.name: Hash and pseudonym attacks
attacks.summary: Unsalted hashes of predictable values can be guessed; stable tokens enable joins.
attacks.implemented: Keyed HMAC pseudonyms, secret not exported, retained-identifier warnings.
attacks.mitigation: Use appropriate key management; avoid unnecessary cross-release stability.
attacks.limitation: HMAC does not anonymize other fields or conceal duplicate frequencies.

attacks.name: Row order and hidden correspondence
attacks.summary: Unchanged ordering can reveal a direct original-to-release mapping.
attacks.implemented: Output rows shuffled by default; scoring lineage never exported.
attacks.mitigation: Remove row numbers and inherited export metadata.
attacks.limitation: Other attributes may still align rows, and audit reports are sensitive.

attacks.name: Date and trajectory linkage
attacks.summary: A distinctive sequence of dates can identify someone even after shifting.
attacks.implemented: Date year extraction and optional per-subject offsets.
attacks.mitigation: Review temporal patterns and clinical intervals explicitly.
attacks.limitation: Sequence/trajectory attacks are not implemented.

attacks.name: Genomic and family inference
attacks.summary: Genomes and relatives create identification routes that ordinary table checks miss.
attacks.implemented: Scope warning and specialist-evaluation requirements.
attacks.mitigation: Use domain-specific release review and access restrictions.
attacks.limitation: No genomic safety determination is made.

attacks.name: Location and mobility
attacks.summary: A few distinctive places or routes can connect records to a person.
attacks.implemented: ZIP prefix transform only.
attacks.mitigation: Treat trajectories as high-dimensional identifiers.
attacks.limitation: No GPS/mobility anonymization engine.

attacks.name: Free-text identifiers
attacks.summary: Narratives can identify a person through names, events or unusual details.
attacks.implemented: Regex pattern redaction; Presidio integration plan.
attacks.mitigation: Review with domain-aware tools and human oversight.
attacks.limitation: Regex is not reliable narrative de-identification.

attacks.name: Images, audio and file metadata
attacks.summary: Faces, voices, headers or embedded metadata can disclose identities.
attacks.implemented: Non-CSV formats rejected by the starter workflow.
attacks.mitigation: Use specialist DICOM, image, audio and document pipelines.
attacks.limitation: No OCR, voice anonymization or medical-image scrubber is shipped.

attacks.name: Spreadsheet formula injection
attacks.summary: Untrusted cells can execute spreadsheet formulas when opened.
attacks.implemented: Formula-leading cells and headers neutralized on export by default.
attacks.mitigation: Keep formula-safe export enabled and disclose lexical changes.
attacks.limitation: This is file-handling security, not statistical anonymization.

attacks.name: Audit and selection leakage
attacks.summary: Exact before/after metrics, rare examples or a selected recipe can expose source facts.
attacks.implemented: Owner-only reports, no-store headers, no raw witnesses in release CSV.
attacks.mitigation: Keep diagnostic artifacts confidential; privatize selection if it becomes public.
attacks.limitation: The optimizer is non-DP and does not certify public report release.

attacks.name: Group and inferential harms
attacks.summary: A private individual contribution can coexist with harmful conclusions about a group.
attacks.implemented: Documented release-review criterion.
attacks.mitigation: Evaluate purpose, governance and possible group harms.
attacks.limitation: Individual privacy mechanisms do not erase true population associations.

attacks.name: Sharing authorization and transport
attacks.summary: A protected file can still be sent to the wrong person or over an unsafe channel.
attacks.implemented: Explicit export acknowledgment, no transmission function.
attacks.mitigation: Check permission and use an approved encrypted transfer route.
attacks.limitation: PRISM is not encryption, authorization, or a compliance determination.

methods.name: Drop columns
methods.summary: Remove fields not required by the analysis.
methods.limitation: Exact deletion does not protect remaining combinations.

methods.name: Mask values
methods.summary: Replace a whole column with a constant, including blanks.

methods.name: Keyed pseudonyms
methods.summary: Use HMAC with a fresh secret key for a candidate.
methods.limitation: Reversible mapping is not shipped; correlations and repeated tokens remain.

methods.name: Numeric bands
methods.limitation: Five-year and five-kilogram bands are starting choices, not safety standards.

methods.name: Prefix generalization
methods.summary: Shorten a string such as a ZIP code.
methods.limitation: Three-digit ZIP codes require additional population conditions for HIPAA Safe Harbor.

methods.name: Top / bottom coding
methods.limitation: May distort tail analysis; does not hide all extreme attributes.

methods.name: Rounding
methods.summary: Round to a selected numeric step.
methods.limitation: Round-to-even behavior is explicit; rounding is not formal privacy.

methods.name: Rare-category pooling
methods.summary: Pool infrequent labels into an OTHER category.
methods.limitation: Pooling may erase scientifically important minorities.

methods.name: Year-only dates
methods.limitation: Other dates, ages and unusual event patterns still matter.

methods.name: Consistent date offsets
methods.summary: Apply a secret per-entity date offset.
methods.limitation: Relative intervals remain and can identify a trajectory; not DP.

methods.name: Numeric perturbation
methods.limitation: No privacy accounting or DP guarantee; may create implausible values.

methods.name: Column shuffling
methods.summary: Permute selected values while preserving the marginal distribution.
methods.limitation: Can destroy correlations and may leave many unchanged cells.

methods.name: Pattern redaction
methods.limitation: Does not cover all narrative identifiers.

methods.name: Small-class suppression
methods.summary: Remove complete rows below a requested k under selected fields.
methods.limitation: Subject-unit and suppressed-cohort bias need review; no attribute-disclosure guarantee.

methods.name: ARX privacy models
methods.summary: Vetted generalization search, microaggregation and richer constraints.
methods.limitation: Java worker is not integrated in this delivery.

methods.name: Differentially private aggregates
methods.summary: Optional OpenDP primitive with explicit adjacency and charge.
methods.limitation: Demo accountant is not persistent or production-ready.

methods.name: Synthetic generation
methods.limitation: No neural generation, training job, or synthetic privacy claim in this prototype.
